### Pressure Vessels
### Safety
- Identify contents prior to application of water onto exposed surface as water can cause heat reaction
- Possible BLEVE
### Considerations
- Consider site evacuation
- Consider utilising TIC
### Actions
- Liaise with onsite specialist
- Secure the scene
- Protect exposures and contain
- Attempt to control with fuel isolation or dry agents
- Liaise with onsite specialist

Ascertain:
- Vessel contents
- Can the vessel be isolated/turned off?
- Can the vessel be depressurised?
### Specialist contacts / Notifications
Plant Managers, operators and onsite specialist

NOTIFY – WorkSafe Victoria

### Flammable Metals
### Safety
- Exercise extreme caution due to: Possible spontaneous heating or combustion
- High risk of explosion for metal dust or powder
- Storage potentially being in flammable liquid – kerosene,
### Actions
**DO NOT USE WATER** as extinguishing agent – creates violent reaction

### Gas Flare Off - LPG
Able to flare-off LPG cylinders (vehicle and other) **up to 200kg**.

LPG flare-off operation is to be implemented at incidents involving leaking LPG cylinders, where the **leak cannot be isolated**.
### Considerations
- Location of incident for evacuation and possible **ignition sources**
- Cylinder size – **max 200kg**
- Flare-off operations can only take place with a minimum of **two gas flare-off operators** on scene
- Atmospheric monitoring equipment to determine flammability
- VicPol and Ambulance Victoria response

### Gas Mains / Natural Gas
ACTIONS
### With Fire ...GAAS
- **G**as Company for **IMMEDIATE** response
- **A**pproach from safe direction
- **A**scertain whether supply can be **shut off**
- Protect **exposures**
### Without Fire ...GEtFUQD
- **G**as Company for **IMMEDIATE** response
- **E**liminate ignition sources **30mts** minimum
- (t)
- **F**ully charged **line**. Dissipate gas in exceptional circumstances
- **U**pwind approach with **appropriate** PPC
- **Q**REA for gas monitoring
- **D**rychem on standby
### Inside/Confined Space
- **Evacuate**
- Use personal **gas monitor** to monitor gas **concentration** (%LEL)
- **Ventilate** until **personal** gas monitor **alarm** ceases
- Shut off **gas** when **safe** to do so

### Major Hazardous Facilities / Refineries
### Actions — FFLLEES BMW(M)
- **FIRST APPLIANCE** on scene report to INCIDENT SUPPORT CENTRE
- **FOLLOWING APPLIANCES** report to STAGING AREA
- **LOCATE** and ACCESS emergency information container (front gate/nr entrance)
- **LIASE** with on-site EMERGENCY SUPERVISOR
- **ESTABLISH LOCATION** and access to fire/spill
- **EVACUATE** area
- **SEND** regular sitreps
- **BOOST** hydrants/sprinklers
- **MAINTAIN** appliance FLASHING lights in MHF
- **WEAR** ear/eye protection
- **MONITOR** wind direction/weather reports

### Electrical
### Aerial Appliances - Safety
- Use a **spotter** near powerline ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Clearance for EWP **3m** no go zone **poles**
- **8m** no go zone **Towers**
### Electrical Substations / Substation yards ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- **Firefighters** shall not **enter** unless **accompanied** by an electrical supply **company representative** or other **trained/authorised** persons.

### Pole Fires – Actions ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- **Power Co.** requested immediately
- Do not attempt **extinguish** until power company confirm **isolation** or confirm area safe before extinguishing
- Protect **exposures**
- Attack fire **ONLY** to protect life by;
  - **Fog** or broken stream (no jet)
  - **Lob** onto fire
  - Avoid **wires**
  - Don't **stand** in water/wet surfaces
### Uninterrupted Power Supplies (UPS)
Treat as live, isolate power between electrical equipment and UPS, ESC to respond to ensure power is isolated
- UPS may be present when dealing with **computers**, **telephone exchanges**, **process controllers**.
- Treat all such **equipment** as **live**.
- **Isolate** power between **electrical equipment** and **UPS**.
- Request power supply company to **respond** to ensure power **isolation**

### Fire Investigation
### Response Criteria of Fire Investigators
- All **fire** related **deaths**
- All **fire** related **serious** injuries
- Fires where the **origin** and cause cannot be easily **determined**
- Notification at **3rd alarm** and **automatic** FIA response at **4th alarm** or greater at structure fires (MFB)
- Any firefighter **injury** (MFB)
- Fires involving fire brigade **property**
- MFB Fire Investigation will not attend **suspicious** fires unless **requested** by **VicPol**
### Considerations
- Obstacles preventing entry into building access/firefighting
- Extent of fire on arrival
- locations / intensity / colour of flames/smoke
- Indications of forcible entry
- Conditions of doors / windows

### LPG
### Properties
- DG IERG GUIDE 04
- UN **1075** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- HAZCHEM: **2YE**
- Exp ratio **270:1**
- LEL **1.5%** UEL **10%**

### LPG (Properties, continued)
- **Heavier** than air, will collect in low areas
- LPG cylinder **silver**, bullets **White**

### Hospitals
### Actions
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Code RED | Fire, smoke |
| Code PURPLE | Bomb threat, extortion, suspicious package |
| Code ORANGE | Evacuation |
| Code YELLOW | Explosion, person trapped, chemical emergency |
| Code GREY | Patient violent, patient restraint |
| Code BLACK | Non patient violence, armed/unarmed intrusion, armed patient violence |
| Code BLUE | Medical emergency |
| Code BROWN | State disaster, major incident, internal accident |

**Code Black** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM

### Electric and hybrid vehicles
### Actions
- Approach from side
- Chock wheels, apply park brake
- Place transmission into Park
- Stabilise if not on four wheels
- ***Note:*** *After disabling the HV battery pack, power is maintained for 90 seconds in the airbags and up to 10 minutes in the high voltage electrical system.* ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
### Generic Information for all motor vehicle incidents/fires
### Considerations
- Availability of water supply (respond WT or PT if req)
- Fuel Source (petrol, gas, elec...)
- Undeployed airbags
- Once 12v battery is disconnected, handbrake may not engage/disengage

### LPG powered vehicles
### Safety
- Do **not extinguish** burning if **gas** still **venting**; **LEAVE TO BURN**
- Be aware of **increase** in **fire intensity/ pitch** of escaping gas; **SITUATION DETERIORATING**
- **EVACUATE** if suspected of rupturing
- Do not direct water at **VENTING PRESSURE GAUGE** - icing
### Actions
**During Fire**
- Utilize hose lines from **SHELTERED POSITION** where possible
- Cool cylinder with flooding quantities of water onto upper surfaces until **well after** fire is out
- Use dry chem, CO2 or water spray to **EXT FIRE** (only if **absolutely necessary** AND **safe to do so**)

### Non-structure fires - Rubbish Tips and other waste storage sites
### Notifications ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- Council MERO
- EPA
- DoH
- Vic WorkCover Authority
- Ops Comm
- Comm Resilience Comm

- Fire Safety Issue notification (completed to ensure notification of Building Inspection and compliance dept)

### Secured Facility Response ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
### Actions
- Meet with facility Liaison Officer (LO) and Field Comm (FC) at entrance to site
- OIC to ascertain nature and status of event, status of secured facility and assess situation
- Enter on only req by Facility Management, if site security is confirmed, and only under guidance of escort/liaison officer (one per appl)
- If req to enter and is deemed safe to do so, and if need arises, IC notify Ops Comm
- FSV personnel to receive briefing by facility staff incl arrangements for emerg evac plan
- Min number of appl and crew to be committed, IC to determine
- Routine security checks undertaken in consideration of situation
- FSV to withdraw if safety/security of personnel/appl becomes threatened
- Security checks on departure. LO to confirm absence of prisoners on appl
- IC to confirm ID of FF leaving secured Facility
### High rise buildings
### Considerations
- **EVACUATE** (floor and roof area)- EWIS control- location of fire exit stairs
- **TACTICAL FIRE** plans / **floor plans / MSDS**
- **COMMUNICATION PLAN**
- **ESTABLISH SECTORS** (Sector 2-16)
- Use of manned **FIREFIGHTER LIFT**
- Establish **FALLING DEBRIS** perimeter

### High rise buildings (continued)
High rise (**25m +**) – utilize **BOOSTERS** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM

If a building is **ULTRA HIGH RISE** (**50 + stories/ 150m +**)
- **REFUGE ZONES** may be present on **HIGHER FLOORS** to aid **EVACUATION**
### Safe Working at Heights
### Considerations
- Respond **H**ART
- Utilising **A**erial appliance
- Separate **R**adio channel for SWH operations
- **T**IC for roof temperature

### Docks/Ports
### Safety
Waterway **SAFETY** is always **P E A C E**
- **P**FD within 2mts of edge
- **E**stablish 2mt safety zone around edges
- **A**ppoint Safety Officer
- **C**aution working near edges
- b**E**ware of load limitations on piers/jetties/wharves...
  - No **weight limit plaque** = **NO GO**
### Considerations
- Marine operators responded
- Beware of weight limitations/loading on wharves and appliance exclusion zones.
- TUGS available west of Bolte Bridge only
- **SHIPPING container NUMBER** – obtain container number and relay to firecom for details of contents
  - 2 - 4 alpha characters followed by 6-7 numeric characters
  - **Number marked on all sides of container** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM

### Actions (SLAM) ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- **S**eek specialist advise
- **L**iaise with port authority personnel
- **A**wareness of other vehicles in dock area
- **M**aintain flashing lights at all times
### Ship emergencies/Firefighting tugs
### Actions
- Respond **FIRE BOATS (FRV)**
- Respond **COAST GUARDS (CFA)**
- Establish and maintain contact with **SHIPS SENIOR OFFICER** on board
- Report to the **SHIPS BRIDGE**
- Determine **LOCATION** and **ACCESS** to fire & intensity
- Access information
  - **SHIPS PLANS**
  - **FIREFIGHTING** already **UNDERTAKEN**
  - Operation of **FIREFIGHTING INSTALLATION/EQUIPMENT**
  - Details of **CARGO / MANIFEST / LOG**
  - State of **SHIPS SERVICES** power & water
  - **VENTILATION**
  - **SHIPS STABILITY**
  - State of ships **HATCHES**
  - Fire **SERVICE VESSELS** or **FIRE TUGS** to **COOL** the **EXTERIOR** of the vessel

### Ship emergencies/Firefighting tugs (continued)
  - **MONITOR AMOUNT** of water used and **REMOVAL** of firefighting water (**STABILITY**)
  - Establish **ORIGIN** of **IGNITION**
  - Consider & monitor **ALTERNATIVE EXTINGUISHING** media
### Pollution Control
### Considerations - SCARS
- **S**ize, location & **type** of **spill**
- Identify **C**ontrol agency
- **A**ccessing State Cache of equipment
- **R**espond (WR) Waterways Emergency responder
- **S**pecialist advice early on

### Trams
### Considerations
- Trams operate **600V** DC tractive control from overhead trolley wire
- **POWER CONTROL CENTRAL** able to ISOLATE POWER TO SECTIONS of the network remotely.
- **ISOLATION** not guaranteed until maintenance crews arrive
- Respond **Heavy Rescue Pod**
- Tram roof = **HART**

### Victoria Police
### MERC ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (who is responsible for rehousing)
**M**UNICIPAL **E**MERGENCY **R**ESPONSE **C**OORDINATOR
- VicPol **District Senior Sergeant** (MERC) has the responsibility to **coordinate requests from the Fire Services**, including but not limited to **accommodation, logistics, support resources** or issues related to **recovery activities**. (continues p.43)

*(MERC continued from p.42)* ...limited to **accommodation, logistics, support resources** or issues related to **recovery activities**.
### Airwing Authorisation/Guidelines
AIR WING AUTHORISATION ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Requests for **Victorian Police** air **support** in **emergency** situations may be made through the on-scene **VicPol coordinator**
### Hostile Acts
### Siting of Appliances PUPMAN
HOSTILE ACT - SIGHTING APPLIANCE
- **P**ark minimum 300m from area
- **U**tilise open space wherever possible
- **P**ark appliance facing away
- **N**otify firecom of location of appliance
- **A**ll firefighters stay in rear seats, side windows open
- **M**aintain clear access and egress at all times

or

ONLY THE FIRST TWO APPLIANCES ARE TO RESPOND TO THE SCENE, ALL FURTHER APPLIANCES ARE TO STAGE A SAFE DISTANCE AWAY
